**Reasoning:**

I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. I am 70 now, my back is not what it was, and my son works in Shijiazhuang. I have about 5 mu of flat land. I know what works here.

Winter wheat and summer maize — that is what I grow. I have done this rotation for forty years. The soil knows it, I know it, and the grain station buys it without trouble. Cotton used to pay more but the picking is backbreaking and I cannot manage it alone anymore. I am not going to try peanuts or vegetables on a large scale at my age. Too much uncertainty and too much bending.

For wheat, I will plant an improved variety — the seed from the cooperative in the county town, something like Jimai. I have used it before and it does well. I apply compound fertilizer before planting and urea at the jointing stage. I have to irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I cannot afford to gamble on rain here — the aquifer is still there and I pay for the pump. Herbicide once in spring and a fungicide spray when the weather turns humid near harvest to keep rust away. The tractor hire does the rotary tillage before planting.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. No-tillage — the machine plants directly into the stubble and I save a step. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar, whatever the shop has. I put compound fertilizer in at planting and chase it with urea when the plants are knee-high. One irrigation if July is dry. Herbicide once, spray for corn borer once.

That is the whole year.
